thread:
Maria Chen: seeing a big spike in kv-cache size + streaming stalls on prod-rtg-*. Alerts firing: paging.evictions and stream.token_cadence>threshold. Customers reporting stalled streams. Investigating.

OpsBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created INC-1965 - kv-cache growth + partial streaming stall. Severity: HIGH. Pager: oncall-sre. Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-1965

oncall-sre: on it. quick question — is this isolated to a single shard / region?

Eric Patel: metrics first pass: prometheus shows sustained kv_cache_entries_total increase starting 2026-03-15T03:22Z, batch size distribution shifted up (more large batches). We also see streaming_token_cadence p95 spike ~ 1.2s -> 4.6s for 5% of requests.

Sasha Ivanov: past week we rolled new batching heuristics (auto_expand=true) in canary. Did that hit prod fully?

Joel Rivera: last deploy was a weekend canary promotion 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC — auto_expand was enabled for runtime-v3 by default. That could let batch sizes grow uncontrolled for low-latency short sequences.

Aisha Khan: logs show repeated KV cache misses then rapid insert churn, causing paging thrash. Sample from prod logs: ```
[2026-03-15T03:25:12Z] INFO shard=rtg-17 kv_cache_insert key=ctx:ab12 size=8192 total_entries=1_234_567
[2026-03-15T03:25:12Z] WARN shard=rtg-17 paging_eviction_count=120 eviction_rate=0.45
[2026-03-15T03:25:13Z] ERROR shard=rtg-17 stream_flush_partial seq=514 lag_ms=3400
```

Eric Patel: quick check commands I ran: ```bash
# top offending shards by kv growth
curl -sS 'https://prom/redwood/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(kv_cache_inserts[5m])) by (shard)' | jq
# streaming cadence samples
curl -sS 'https://prom/redwood/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(stream_token_cadence_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,shard))' | jq
```

Sasha Ivanov: hypothesis: auto_expand allowed continuous batching to increase batch_size for certain request patterns which enlarged in-memory KV references, pushing eviction and causing partial flush bugs in streaming path under eviction backpressure.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan proposal (quick hitters): 1) revert auto_expand on runtime-v3 to previous caps 2) enable conservative kv eviction TTL 3) throttle continuous batching for high-rate shards 4) perform controlled restart of rtg pods on top offending shards. Any objections?

Maria Chen: agree. customer-impact: CS reports 3 customers with degraded streaming (stalls + reconnects) — low volume but higher error latency for real-time sessions. Need customer comms draft.

DeployBot: rolling config change queued: runtime-v3.auto_expand=false on cluster prod-rtg. Approving deploy... :white_check_mark: started canary on rtg-01, rtg-02.

Eric Patel: applying kv eviction TTL as a hotpatch: ```yaml
runtime_kv_cache:
  eviction_ttl_seconds: 120
  max_entries: 600000
```
Patched on canary shards. Monitoring.

Aisha Khan: observed immediate drop in kv_cache_entries_total on canary after TTL applied (~20% reduction) and stream token cadence p95 improved from 4.6s -> 1.1s on canary.

oncall-sre: proceeding to restrict continuous batching throttle for shards with rate > 200 rps: config change: `batching.continuous.max_batch_size=32` and `batching.continuous.window_ms=25`. Applying to prod-rtg in rolling fashion.

Joel Rivera: note — there's known partial-flush issue when eviction interrupts `stream.flush()` leading to duplicate partial commits. Patch branch ready: fix/partial-flush-guard (prevents eviction during critical region). I can cut a hotfix release if needed.

Maria Chen: prioritize config changes first to reduce immediate customer impact. If partial flush errors persist after throttles, cut hotfix.

Customer Success Bot: CS-1729 opened for impacted customers, notifying account owners: "We are investigating intermittent streaming stalls; mitigation in progress. ETA next update in 30m."

OpsBot: Metrics alert correlation: paging.evictions decreased from 3200/min -> 480/min on canary after changes. Streaming error rate for affected endpoints down 70%.

Eric Patel: logs after reload on canary: ```
[2026-03-15T03:40:01Z] INFO shard=rtg-02 batching.max_batch=32 continuous=true
[2026-03-15T03:40:03Z] INFO shard=rtg-02 kv_eviction_ttl=120 total_entries=980_123
[2026-03-15T03:40:05Z] INFO shard=rtg-02 stream_flush ok seq=620
```

Sasha Ivanov: suggest we leave TTL + max_batch for 6 hours and monitor region-wide before reverting code change. Also kick off job to backfill postmortem prompts/trace IDs for affected streams.

oncall-sre: performing rolling restart of rtg pods on top 5 offending shards now (expected ~12m per shard). Notifying on-call rotation.

Maria Chen: customer impact update to CS: "We deployed throttles and eviction TTLs; early results show significant reduction in stalls. We will keep you updated and follow with post-incident writeup."

Joel Rivera: Heads up — hotfix branch still required to remove partial flush race during eviction. I'll prepare a canary build to validate after stabilization.

Aisha Khan: creating a perf dashboard snapshot and linking to the incident now. https://dashboards.redwood/INC-1965/perf

oncall-sre: handoff note for next oncall (Aisha -> Sasha): keep TTL & batch caps in place. If paging.evictions > 800/min for more than 10m, escalate to eng-runtime. If stream.partial_flush errors reappear, roll back runtime restart and run `kubectl logs --since=15m -l app=rtg -c runtime | grep partial_flush` and tag Joel.

Sasha Ivanov: ack; will pick up at 04:30 UTC. Will coordinate postmortem and RCA with Joel and Eric.

OpsBot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT INC-1965 status -> mitigated. Next steps: follow-up RCA, code hotfix timeline, customer comms, long-term tuning of batch heuristics.

Maria Chen: thanks everyone. Filing a follow-up ticket to evaluate auto_expand heuristics and add safety caps + unit tests to prevent unchecked batch growth.

Customer Success Bot: CS-1729 update sent to customers at 03:58 UTC.

oncall-sre: transferring ownership of incident to Sasha for RCA and postmortem. leaving detailed notes in INC-1965. Handoff complete. :wave:
